data.narrative:
Corvex Systems is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Jason Blick that has raised $5M+. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of eight private robotics companies and one public comparable (277810.KQ), though the private peer set includes names such as Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Bedrock Robotics.

Of the two methods examined, only stage-progression proved applicable. The peer-median approach was not feasible due to insufficient narrow-filter comparables—while eight same-sector peers exist in robotics and manufacturing, the dataset contained only one same-stage peer and zero adjacent-stage or similar-valuation-tier peers, falling short of the three-datapoint minimum needed for reliable calibration. The stage-progression method applies a 2.5x multiplier to the $5M total raised proxy, implying a valuation of $12.5M and reflecting typical Seed to next-stage step-up dynamics.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $11M to $14M, centered on $12.5M. This range incorporates modest sensitivity around the 2.5x step-up assumption. The primary limitation is methodological: reliance on a single triangulation method leaves the valuation vulnerable to stage-progression assumptions that lack peer-derived validation. A fuller assessment would benefit from either closer comparable data at seed or early-stage financials that could anchor revenue multiples or burn-rate analysis.
